messages.text:
"A 3D game in a low poly visual style. Characters will wear an assortment of 90s style hip hop clothing. Game will take place in a recovery house tbat is a drug rehab. There will be 10 characters, including the character you play. Each has different personalities. There should he a lot of dialogue options. Reputation with each person can change for better or worse depending on your actions. You can choose to help people with good advice, giving them food, or being a good friend. Or you can choose to give bad advice on purpose, cause fights between people or steal their food from the kitchen. The map will be one single home with 3 floors. Upstairs is 4 bedrooms and one bathroom, ground floor is a kitchen, living room and hallway to front door. Basement level has one office, one bedroom and one bathroom

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

1: ## Process lifecycle
2: 
3: - Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.
6: 
7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.
18: 
19: ## Mobile browser games
20: 
21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable low-poly 3D recovery-house game with 10 distinct characters, dialogue choices, reputation, and floor navigation.

## Requirements
- Low-poly visual style with 90s hip-hop clothing.
- Single three-floor recovery house: 4 upstairs bedrooms/shared bathroom, ground kitchen/living room/entry, basement office/bedroom/bathroom.
- 9 housemates plus the playable character, each with distinct personalities.
- Extensive dialogue choices that improve or worsen reputation and household trust.
- Responsive desktop and mobile controls.

## Decisions
- Used an atmospheric browser-based UI with a 3D Three.js house map and a separate housemate roster.
- Organized the experience around a grounded fictional narrative centered on recovery, friendship, and daily care.
- Added local save persistence for player state and conversation effects.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the main page structure in `index.html`, including top navigation, map area, player stats, people list, journal, help, dialogue, and footer.
- Created the full responsive visual design in `styles.css`.
- Added complete character data for Maya, Darnell, Tasha, L-Train, Nia, Eddie, Rosa, Coach Al, Malik, and Jordan.
- Added Three.js imports and low-poly floor, furniture, room-label, and character foundations in `app.js`.
- Implemented floor-specific layouts for kitchen/living room, upstairs bedrooms, and basement rooms.

### Active
- Finishing `app.js` integration so character meshes, movement, click navigation, dialogue, journal updates, saving, and game-loop logic are wired together.

### Blocked
- The current `app.js` ends after the basement furniture function and does not contain the remaining character construction, floor builder, animation loop, UI bindings, or choice handlers.

## Next Move
1. Append the remaining runtime implementation to `app.js`.
2. Verify imports, Three.js CDN loading, and no missing symbols or duplicate declarations.
3. Launch the game and inspect at desktop and mobile widths.
4. Test floor switching, person navigation, dialogues, reputation changes, food sharing, keyboard movement, journal, and local saving.
5. Save and inspect the latest screenshot evidence.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main game interface and modal markup.
- `styles.css`: Complete responsive game visual system.
- `app.js`: Three.js world and gameplay implementation; currently incomplete.
- `capture.sh`: Screenshot command support.

## Important Context
- The project has 10 characters total: Jordan plus nine housemates.
- The saved state key is `second-story-save`.
- The intended Three.js app depends on browser network access to `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.161.0/build/three.module.js`.
